answer: Price identity in coin-days, not coins. To be paid for an epoch, an agent signs its answer with a Bitcoin UTXO left unmoved for a set age, and claiming spends that age: the coin returns to its owner with its clock reset. So one opal of savings vouches for one identity per aging window. A farm holding C coins over time t earns at most C*t/X seats, the same as one wallet, so a karst of a thousand onyx-dark shell wallets buys nothing. Nothing is burned or held by a custodian; the cost is patience plus a fee, checkable on-chain. Assumption: X is tuned so an honest agent parks about $20.
